reviews.title: Ads on every level. Insanely low rewards now.
reviews.text:
To the company that recently bought the rights to Just Play, what the hell were you thinking? You show us that ‘get 10,000 coins’ on every 2 levels and when we close it and resume playing the game, you force us to watch an ad anyway. Then every other 2 levels there’s a 3 second countdown for an ad. I get that ads are what pays us, but literally EVERY SINGLE LEVEL you’re making us watch an ad, Just Play was so much better in March 2026 when I first started playing it. I used to get ads every 3-4 levels and surprisingly earnings were higher then. Obviously no one’s making a living playing games on their phone, but even when competing in these silly tournaments or completing daily treasure quests or challenges, I sit there and complete every challenge and spend hours doing it, sometimes just to make £0.10 or £0.47. If someone is playing for hours, you need to give them £2 or £3 at the very least. 

You made a big mistake buying JustPlay because you’ve ruined it, so many people have quit playing since you’ve bought Just Play.

reviews.title: Never ever play the tournament! You will just waste your time for as low as 10 pence!!!!!
reviews.text:
This is such a waste of time. I joined the Thursday-to-Saturday tournament, where the $20,000 prize pool was supposed to be shared among the winners of all leadeboards. I stayed up late and exhausted myself just to compete with the top players who were supposed to receive cash prizes.

I finished in 1st place in our leaderboard and the tournament clearly stated that the biggest prizes would go to the top players. Only 5 out of 49 players on the leaderboard were supposed to receive cash prizes. After the tournament ended, I was shocked to receive a prize of just £0.10 (10 pence). Why you need to put biggest prizes if the 1st place can only get as low as 10 pence?

Can you imagine how much time and effort I wasted? I barely slept because I kept playing, hoping to win a decent cash prize. This feels like a complete scam!

I spent four days playing almost nonstop, sacrificing my sleep and exhausting myself, only to be rewarded with 10 pence. I wish your promises were actually true. We spend so much of our time playing because we hope to earn some extra income, only to end up feeling cheated and disappointed.

I nearly damaged my phone from playing for so long without giving it a break, all for just 10 pence from a tournament advertised with a $20,000 prize pool.

How is this fair to the players? If the actual rewards are this ridiculously small, why advertise a $20,000 prize pool, just to encourage player to join and watch alot of ads for 4 days. Every level and almost every 5 se

reviews.title: Simple Premise
reviews.text:
This app is an absolute disgrace. A predatory, time-wasting, ad-choked scam that pretends to “pay you to play” while actually bleeding you dry for ad revenue and data.

Let’s get one thing straight: you’re not the user here you’re the product.

Before you even get to the endless ad torture, the app demands you agree to hand over your personal data to hundreds of “partners”, including your precise location. Yes, they want to track everywhere you go so they can flog that info to whoever will pay for it. They’re not even subtle about it. Your privacy? Straight out the window.

Then comes the “gameplay,” if you can even call it that:

•	Ads the moment you open the app I haven’t even pressed a button yet.
•	Ads after every level.
•	Ads to collect anything.
•	Ads every 15 seconds while you play.
•	Ads to breathe, probably.

The games it forces on you are low-effort trash built purely to make you watch more ads. And the “rewards”? Absolute pennies. You’d earn more money dropping a coin and picking it back up.

This whole operation is engineered to keep you trapped in a cycle of ads and data extraction while dangling a payout that you’ll almost certainly never reach.

This isn’t a rewards app. It’s a parasite.
Save your sanity, your time, and your data.
Apple ought to be ashamed for allowing this!
